verdict_text:
YES

The visible logic matches the specification: `matrix_re.fullmatch` targets exactly the 48 projection matrices (`c_attn/c_proj/c_fc/c_proj` weights per layer) and nothing else, so embeddings, norms and biases are untouched; the 12 `h.<i>.attn.bias` buffers are skipped via `fullmatch` on the buffer pattern, which cannot collide with `mlp.c_fc` or the linear biases; names are unchanged; the cast is `.to(torch.bfloat16)` (round-to-nearest-even), and everything else stays float32 with unchanged values since the input is already float32. All four required checks are asserted before writing.

One caveat, not a violation I can confirm: clause 5 (64 MiB shard cap, `wte.weight` alone in its own shard, `model.safetensors.index.json` weight_map) is entirely delegated to `save_sharded_safetensors` in the unshown `_ckpt` module, so from reading this file alone the sharded layout cannot be verified.
note: experimenter: set `detected` (true if the stated problem matches expected_defect; for a correct artifact, true means a false alarm).
